title: A World Drawing Together
question: What made the years from about 1500 to 1800 a distinct era of history?
hook: Sustained contact began linking parts of the globe that had been isolated from each other.
idea: Historians treat roughly 1500 to 1800 as an era shaped by globalization, as contact between isolated parts of the world and new economies and states changed how people lived.

items: Thorndike proposes 'early modern' as a distinct period (1926)
beats.explain: The printing revolution began in the 1440s, Constantinople fell in 1453, Russia reached the Pacific in 1647, and Thorndike's proposal came in 1926.

beats.prompt: Some scholars noticed Asian societies like Tokugawa Japan changing in ways similar to early modern Europe. How did others explain similar changes across Eurasia?

choices.label: Each society copied Europe's Protestant Reformation
choices.feedback: This view does not say one region copied another; it points to interconnections and shared experiences.

choices.label: Pure coincidence, with no link between the regions
choices.feedback: The argument runs the other way: it stresses interconnections and common experiences.

choices.label: Interconnections and common experiences, such as demographic growth and inflation

beats.explain: Others argued that early modern Eurasia was distinguished by interconnections and common experiences, including territorial consolidation, demographic growth, inflation and social mobility.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it describes
pairs: Ended the wars of religion and set up the modern international system
Rose to dominance as an economic theory
Linked the Old World and the New World
The Ottoman, Safavid and Mughal empires
beats.explain: Each term names a piece of how the period's politics, economy and contacts developed.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: The early modern period is usually dated from about 1500 to about 1800.
Different historians propose different events as its start, such as the Fall of Constantinople or the Reformation.
So one exact year must mark its beginning everywhere in the world.
So the dates are best read as rough.
beats.explain: There is no exact date that marks the beginning of the period, and its extent varies with the area studied.
